title: Active incidence and comma-cone comparisons for operadic families
statement:
Use the small families, their fiberwise inert edges and incidence cones of [def-coef-operadic-correspondence], monoidal infinity categories of [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category], joins of [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone], and coherent functors of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $n\geq1$ and $\pi:\mathcal P\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\times\Delta^n$ be a family whose restrictions to all parameter edges are constant over $[0]$ and whose zero-fibers are spaces. Require the inert lifts over $(\alpha,\operatorname{id}_t)$ to be $\pi$-cocartesian in the whole family, not only cocartesian after restriction to a parameter fiber; these are the stationary inert lifts used below. Put $\mathcal A=\mathcal P_0$. For an object $b\in\mathcal P_t$, $t>0$, put $J_b=\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal P}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{act}})_{/b}$. For a simplex $\sigma:\Delta^d\to\mathcal P_{\{1,\ldots,n\}}$ consisting of active arrows, define $X_\sigma=\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal P}\mathcal P_{/\sigma}$: its $k$-simplices are maps $\Delta^k\star\Delta^d\to\mathcal P$ equal to $\sigma$ on the last factor and lying in $\mathcal A$ on the first factor. Let $X_\sigma^{\mathrm a}\subseteq X_\sigma$ require every mixed edge from the first factor to the first vertex of $\sigma$ to be active.

(i) If $b$ lies over $[r]$ and $b_1,\ldots,b_r$ are its consecutive inert edge restrictions, cutting the source tuple along the inert projections gives an equivalence $J_b\simeq\prod_{i=1}^rJ_{b_i}$. For every inert-preserving $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal V^\otimes$ this equivalence identifies the source diagram, together with its base map to $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$, with concatenation of the source diagrams on the $J_{b_i}$. These comparisons also identify induced cones whenever the inert projections of $b$ and of their source tuples are preserved. For $r=0$, $J_b$ is contractible and its source diagram is the empty tuple. These comparisons include the common endpoints of adjacent inputs; no discreteness of the zero-fibers is required.

(ii) Restriction to the first vertex gives a trivial Kan fibration $X_\sigma^{\mathrm a}\to J_{\sigma(0)}$. Here trivial Kan fibration means right lifting against every simplicial boundary, including dimension zero.

(iii) Let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal V^\otimes$ be inert-preserving and $f:X_\sigma\to\mathcal V^\otimes$ its composite with source evaluation. For a diagram $g:T\to E$, write $E_{g/}$ for the join coslice, whose $k$-simplices are extensions $T\star\Delta^k\to E$ of $g$. With $p:\mathcal V^\otimes\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ and $f^{\mathrm a}=f|_{X_\sigma^{\mathrm a}}$, the restriction map
$$ (\mathcal V^\otimes)_{f/}\longrightarrow(\mathcal V^\otimes)_{f^{\mathrm a}/}\times_{(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})_{pf^{\mathrm a}/}}(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})_{pf/} $$
is a trivial Kan fibration. Thus prescribed simplices and all their boundaries in these coslices lift with exactly the specified base and restrictions. This compares only these source-comma diagrams with their active parts; it does not identify an operadic colimit with a colimit relative to the whole projection $p$.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 3.1.2.3, step (1), printed pp. 336–337: active-part coslice comparison, restriction to the first vertex, and the product over inert outputs. GH Theorem A.3.4 specifies the generalized nonsymmetric extension: use incidence diagrams including endpoints, with the constant Kan zero-fiber condition. Nonsymmetric formulation following Gepner–Haugseng, arXiv:1312.3178v4 Appendix A. Read online; archive WANTED. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical fact. Family convention checked against HA Definition 2.3.2.10(a): inert lifts stationary in the parameter are cocartesian for the whole family projection. The explicit global condition is needed for the active-source reflection, not inferred from the fiberwise condition alone.

proof.text:
Prove (i) using the family incidence axiom, without any space hypothesis on the one-fibers. Write the inert vertex restrictions of b as v_0,...,v_r. For each v_j the category C_j of arrows a_0 to v_j across the parameter edge 0 to t, with a_0 in A_[0], is contractible and is a space: constancy over [0] identifies it with the slice of the space A_[0] over a chosen inverse image of v_j. Its contraction is composition to the identity arrow of that inverse image; all its arrows are equivalences since A_[0] is a space. This description also applies to diagrams of such arrows. In particular the choices of an identification between two endpoint lifts, compatible with their arrows to v_j, form a contractible space.
For an active arrow u:a to b with base opposite to lambda:[r] to [m], lambda(0)=0 and lambda(r)=m. Put m_i=lambda(i)-lambda(i-1). Restrict a by its stationary inert cocartesian maps to the subintervals [lambda(i-1),lambda(i)]. The cocartesian mapping criterion of [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] factors the composites a to b to b_i through these restrictions, producing active arrows a_i to b_i. It applies across the parameter edge because the stationary inert maps are cocartesian for the whole pi. These factorizations and the same factorizations on coherent triangles give the cutting functor R:J_b to the product of J_{b_i}.
Here is its inverse construction. Given active arrows u_i:a_i to b_i with source lengths m_i, use their endpoint arrows to v_i to identify the final endpoint of a_i with the initial endpoint of a_{i+1} in C_i. The Segal fiber-product equivalence in the generalized-operad definition of [def-coef-operadic-correspondence] glues the a_i to a in A_[m], m=sum_i m_i. For m_i=0 it glues a vertex, with the two endpoint legs retained. Set lambda(j)=sum_{i<=j}m_i. The arrows from a to a_i to b_i and the endpoint arrows now form the full incidence cone over the base map lambda opposite. The relative pi-limit axiom at b in [def-coef-operadic-correspondence] supplies u:a to b, with exactly this cone up to coherent equivalence. Its base is active. Choices in the gluing are contractible relative to the given endpoint and incidence data.
To check morphisms, a triangle in each J_{b_i} includes an active source-change map; write its opposite as h_i between the corresponding input ordinals. Since each h_i preserves endpoints, the translated h_i glue to a unique monotone map h on the concatenated intervals. Endpoint compatibilities lie in the C_i and glue by their contractions. The Segal equivalence for A and the relative pi-limit at b then identify the spaces of these triangles and their compatibility homotopies with the corresponding space for the glued arrow. Apply this argument to coherent diagrams, not only individual triangles: the functor/cone mapping-space calculus of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] tests the same universal properties with any simplicial parameter. Thus gluing gives a coherent inverse to R. Cutting after gluing recovers each u_i; gluing after cutting recovers u by the same Segal and relative-limit universal properties. Their component equivalences are natural equivalences by the cited functor calculus. This proves the equivalence of categories, including arity-changing active source morphisms, rather than merely a product of operation spaces. The zero-output case is dealt with in step 5.

source.place: Theorem 3.1.2.3, step (1), printed pp.336–337, output-product equivalence; generalized nonsymmetric expansion using Gepner–Haugseng Definition A.3.1(2), Definition A.3.2 and Theorem A.3.4.

proof.text: For (ii) take E=P_act and E_0=A_act, the full subcategory of E on the parameter-zero vertices. E is a quasicategory: fill an inner horn in P; for a two-dimensional horn the new edge is the composite of two active base maps and is active, and in higher dimensions all edges are already specified. The subcategory E_0 is full in E since a simplex with all parameter vertices zero lies in A. Identify X_sigma^a with E_0 times_E E_{/sigma}. Indeed an active mixed arrow a to sigma(0), followed by an active arrow of sigma, has active composite. Moreover if h:a to a' is a source edge and both a to sigma(0) and a' to sigma(0) are active, their triangle forces h to be active: on opposite ordinals, composing an endpoint-preserving map with h^op has endpoints 0 and the full input length only if h^op has those endpoints. This includes length zero. The same test on all edges gives the identification on every simplex. Apply [lem-coef-initial-poset-slice-restriction] to T=[d], least element 0, the diagram sigma in E, and this E_0. Its source-restricted target slice is exactly J_{sigma(0)}. It gives the asserted restriction map and lifting of every monomorphism over E_0; in particular every simplicial boundary, including dimension zero, lifts. No left-fibration model of an unspecified extension fiber is used.

source.place: Theorem 3.1.2.3, step (1), printed p.336, first-vertex restriction using the left-anodyne inclusion {B} in sigma; the source-restricted general statement is lem-coef-initial-poset-slice-restriction.

proof.text:
For (iii), first construct the active reflector. The source projection X_sigma to A is the pullback of the right fibration P_{/sigma} to P of [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration], so X_sigma is a quasicategory. Its active part is full: the endpoint calculation of step 2 forces every source edge between active cones to be active. For an object x of X_sigma with initial mixed edge a to sigma(0), let its base be opposite to lambda:[r] to [m]. Factor it by the interval [lambda(0),lambda(r)]: the first base arrow is inert, with opposite j mapping to lambda(0)+j, and the second is active. Lift the first arrow at a by a stationary globally pi-cocartesian edge e:a to a'. Cocartesianness extends the entire cone from a to sigma across e, not just its first edge. Explicitly its outer-horn lifting criterion fills the triangles with e and each edge of the cone and then all higher simplices containing e; the space of compatible factorizations is contractible by [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion]. The resulting cone x' has source a' still in A and every mixed edge active, since the arrows of sigma are active. The factorization gives a unit x to x' in X_sigma.
For an active cone y with source c over [l], a map x to y is a source map h:a to c and the coherent cone triangle. If beta:[r] to [l] is the opposite of the active mixed base map of y, the base triangle says lambda=h^op beta. Since beta preserves endpoints, h^op(0)=lambda(0) and h^op(l)=lambda(r). Monotonicity forces its image into that interval. Consequently h factors uniquely on the base through e by h'^op(j)=h^op(j)-lambda(0). The globally cocartesian mapping criterion gives an equivalence of the spaces of such factorizations including the entire cone triangle. For precision about the slice mapping spaces, [lem-cbc-right-fibration-morphism-space] applied to X_sigma to A expresses them as homotopy fibers of transport of the cone; taking that fiber of the cocartesian mapping equivalence gives Map_{X_sigma^a}(x',y) equivalent to Map_{X_sigma}(x,y), naturally in y. The dual pointwise adjoint criterion [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-adjoint-criterion] therefore assembles x' and these units into a left adjoint to X_sigma^a included in X_sigma.
Apply [lem-coef-cofinal-relative-join-slice-restriction] to this full inclusion, its left adjoint, the inner fibration p:V^tensor to Delta^op supplied by the monoidal definition, and f=F composed with source evaluation. Its displayed right join-coslice restriction is exactly the map in (iii), with f restricted to X_sigma^a. It is a trivial Kan fibration with every prescribed boundary and the entire base fixed. This uses right join-coslices, whose simplices extend X_sigma star Delta^k; it does not use the left-cone comparison on L_tau in the family-cell lemma.

source.place: Theorem 3.1.2.3, step (1), printed p.336: the active full subcategory has a left adjoint, and relative right join-coslice restriction is a trivial Kan fibration. Interval-factorization expansion for the nonsymmetric base and stationary global lifts.

proof.text: Check the diagram and cone compatibility in (i). For an object u:a to b, the cutting construction records the stationary inert maps a to a_i over the consecutive intervals. An inert-preserving F sends each to a p-cocartesian inert map F(a) to F(a_i). By [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category], the Segal coordinates of F(a) are precisely the ordered lists of the Segal coordinates of the F(a_i), in order; its arity is m=sum_i m_i. On a source-change morphism the base map is the glued h of step 1, so the same identification is over Delta^op and agrees with composition. Shared endpoint restrictions were retained in C_i in step 1; applying F sends them to the zero-fiber of V^tensor, which is terminal by the arity-zero Segal condition. Thus the identifications respect both legs at every shared vertex. For an induced cone from an inert-preserving family diagram, its edge to the i-th output is the image of a to b to b_i, factored through a_i. These are exactly the edges and triangles of its factor cones. The relative mapping-space product in the monoidal definition identifies the full cone with this concatenated cone, including its compatibility homotopies. With any simplicial parameter the same coordinate projections identify the transformations and higher simplices, by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. This proves the stated naturality for source diagrams and for induced cones whenever their inert projections are preserved. In (ii) restriction simply deletes the last vertices of sigma; in (iii) restriction simply deletes X_sigma outside its active part. Hence these restriction maps are the specified simplicial maps, independent of the choices made in proving their lifting properties.

source.place: Theorem 3.1.2.3, step (1), printed p.337, identification of the source cocone with the concatenation diagram; generalized incidence endpoints from Gepner–Haugseng Definition A.3.1(2).

proof.text: If r=0, an active base map [m] to [0] has opposite [0] to [m] preserving both endpoints, so m=0. Every object and simplex of J_b therefore lies over [0]. Constancy of the zero-fiber correspondence on the parameter edge 0 to t identifies J_b with the slice of A_[0] over an inverse image of b. That space is contractible by the identity-arrow contraction used in step 1. After F its source lies in V^tensor_[0], the terminal zero-fiber, and is the empty tuple. If r=1, cutting has a single block and both composites of the comparison are the identity up to the universal identifications in step 1. For d=0 the map in (ii) is the identity on J_b; step 3 still applies to the full incoming slice. If J_{sigma(0)} is empty, step 2's map to it forces X_sigma^a to be empty. The reflector of step 3 then forces X_sigma to be empty as well; both relative coslice comparisons reduce to the identity comparison of V^tensor over Delta^op. No nonemptiness hypothesis was inserted. Finally the conclusion of (iii) is solely the relative coslice restriction given in step 3; the definition [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone] imposes no existence of a p-colimit. The whole proof therefore assumes no colimits in V^tensor.

lean.statement: theorem operadic_active_incidence_comparison {n : ℕ} (hn : 1 ≤ n) (P : Family (Δ[n] : SSet.{u})) (hconstant : HasConstantZeroEdges P) (hzero : ∀ z : (Δ[n] : SSet.{u}) _⦋0⦌, KanComplex
